subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The volume of a cube is increasing at the rate of 9 cubic cm/sec. How fast is the surface area increasing when the length of an edge is 10 cm?

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the two formulas you would write, and say which rate you have to find on the way to the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find da/dt from the volume
steps.margin_note: First mark. The volume rate and the surface area rate are not linked directly — the edge rate da/dt is the link between them, so it has to be found first.
lines: Given: dV/dt = 9 cm³/sec.  Asked: dS/dt when a = 10 cm.
Let a be the length of an edge at time t. Then
Differentiate V = a³ with respect to time t:

recall.must_convey: That V = a³ is differentiated with respect to t and solved to give da/dt = 3/100 cm/sec at a = 10.
accept: differentiate v equals a cubed to get d a by d t first
the edge rate connects the volume rate to the area rate
nine equals three hundred times d a by d t
modata d a by d t kanukkovali
da by dt is three by hundred centimetres per second
find the rate of change of the edge from the volume

steps.why: V and S share only one variable, the edge a. Finding da/dt turns the given volume rate into something the surface area formula can use.
common_mistakes: Trying to divide dV/dt by dS/dt directly, with no edge rate in between.
Putting a = 10 into V = a³ before differentiating, which gives dV/dt = 0.
steps.memory_tip: Two formulas, one shared letter. Whatever is given goes in the first formula, whatever is asked comes out of the second, and da/dt is the bridge between them.

steps.label: Differentiate S = 6a² and substitute
steps.margin_note: Second mark. dS/dt = 12a(da/dt). Both a = 10 and the da/dt found above go in here. The unit is cm²/sec, because an area rate is area per second.
lines: Differentiate S = 6a² with respect to time t:

recall.must_convey: That S = 6a² gives dS/dt = 12a(da/dt), and substituting a = 10 with da/dt = 3/100 gives 3.6 cm²/sec.
accept: differentiate six a squared to get twelve a d a by d t
substitute a equal to ten and d a by d t equal to three by hundred
the surface area increases at three point six square centimetres per second
twelve a d a by d t substitute cheste three point six vasthundi
the answer is three point six centimetre square per second
d s by d t is twelve into ten into three by hundred

steps.why: S = 6a² is a function of a alone, so one chain rule step turns it into a time rate. The number 3.6 is only correct with cm²/sec attached, since the same figure would mean something different as a length rate.
common_mistakes: Reusing 9 cm³/sec in place of da/dt in the second formula.
Writing the unit as cm³/sec instead of cm²/sec.
steps.memory_tip: A cube has six equal square faces, so S = 6a², and its derivative doubles the 6 into 12a.

insider_note: Same two-step route as its partner: da/dt from the volume rate, then the surface rate. With a = 10 the numbers stay whole, giving 3.6.
